title: 10.5 Small Group · Group 2
contentObjective: I can create and describe geometric designs using repetition, patterns, and rhythm, and use a pattern unit to predict what comes next, explain how I can tell, and judge a case I have not seen before.
languageObjective: I can justify my answer to a skeptic and connect it to a second strategy or representation.

noticeAndWonder.context: A photograph shows the tiled wall of an old building. The same shapes repeat across it in bands of color — geometric patterns have decorated homes and buildings like this for centuries.
wonderStarters: I wonder what comes next if ___ .
I wonder what math the designer ___ .

turnAndTalk.question: A border repeats pink circle, purple square, blue triangle. Using its pattern unit, how do you predict what shape number 12 is without drawing all 12 shapes?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The pattern unit is 3 shapes long, and 12 ÷ 3 = 4 with no remainder, so shape 12 ends a complete unit — it is the blue triangle.

stems.en: I predict shape 12 by dividing ___ by the ___ length.
stems.es: Predigo la figura 12 al dividir ___ entre la longitud de la ___.

stems.en: Shape 12 is the ___ because the remainder is ___.
stems.es: La figura 12 es el ___ porque el residuo es ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: Using the same pattern, predict shape number 20 — and explain what a remainder of 2 tells you that a remainder of 0 does not.
extendStems: Shape 20 is the ___ because 20 ÷ 3 leaves a remainder of ___.
A remainder of 2 tells me ___, which is different from a remainder of 0 because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: When you sorted design descriptions into 'predictable' and 'rhythm (varies),' what made the circle painting belong with rhythm instead of pattern?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The circle painting's colors, sizes, and ring counts vary with no repeating unit, so it has no predictability the way a pattern does.

stems.en: The circle painting is rhythm because ___.
stems.es: La pintura de círculos es ritmo porque ___.

stems.en: It is not a pattern because it lacks a ___.
stems.es: No es un patrón porque le falta una ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: Could a design have BOTH a pattern and rhythm at the same time, in different parts of the same picture? Give an example to defend your answer.
extendStems: Yes/No, because a design could have a pattern in ___ and rhythm in ___.

turnAndTalk.question: The circle-square-triangle border and a tiled wall border both use pattern units. If a tiled wall's unit is 4 tiles long, how would you predict tile number 25?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Dividing the position number by the pattern unit's length, then reading the remainder, tells you which shape in the unit appears at any position — the method works for any unit length.

stems.en: For the tiled wall, I would divide ___ by ___ to find the remainder.
stems.es: Para el muro de azulejos, dividiría ___ entre ___ para hallar el residuo.

stems.en: This is the same method as the border because both use a ___.
stems.es: Este es el mismo método que el borde porque ambos usan una ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: If tile number 25 in the 4-tile pattern unit design lands on the 1st tile of its unit, what does that tell you about tile number 29? Justify your reasoning.
extendStems: Tile 29 would be the ___ tile in its unit because ___.
I know this because a pattern unit ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice, when a problem asked you to predict a shape at a large position number, what strategy helped you find it quickly?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Dividing the position number by the pattern unit's length and reading the remainder tells you exactly which shape appears there.

stems.en: I found the shape by ___ the position number by the unit's ___.
stems.es: Encontré la figura al ___ el número de posición entre la ___ de la unidad.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who forgot that a remainder of 0 means the LAST shape in the unit, not a new one starting? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

vocabulary.definition: The same object, shape, or form repeated multiple times.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El mismo objeto, figura o forma repetido varias veces.
vocabulary.example: A row of identical squares across a tiled wall.

vocabulary.definition: A set of objects or shapes that are repeated and arranged in a regular order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un conjunto de objetos o figuras que se repiten y se organizan en un orden regular.
vocabulary.example: Circle, square, triangle — circle, square, triangle — again and again.

vocabulary.definition: The smallest chunk of a pattern that repeats.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La parte más pequeña de un patrón que se repite.
vocabulary.example: In circle-square-triangle repeated, the pattern unit is those three shapes.

vocabulary.definition: A design element created by varying the placement, size, orientation, or order of the same objects or shapes.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un elemento de diseño creado al variar la posición, el tamaño, la orientación o el orden de los mismos objetos o figuras.
vocabulary.example: Circles of different sizes and colors scattered with a flow, like in a painting.

vocabulary.definition: Being able to know what comes next because the design follows a rule.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Poder saber qué viene después porque el diseño sigue una regla.
vocabulary.example: Repetition and patterns have it; rhythm often lacks it.

launch.narrative: This is your challenge small group for Lesson 10.5. You can already get the answer — so in here the answer is the starting point. We ask when the method holds, when it breaks, and how you would convince someone who disagrees.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — Repetition, pattern, and rhythm
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Math can be used to create beautiful designs. These designs often have repetition, patterns, and rhythm — and the pattern unit lets you predict what comes next — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

iDo.title: Watch me use a pattern unit
lines: A border repeats: pink circle, purple square, blue triangle, pink circle, purple square, blue triangle, ...
The pattern unit is 3 shapes long: circle, square, triangle.
To predict shape number 12, I divide: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 with no remainder, so shape 12 ends a complete unit — it is the blue triangle.
The next three shapes after any complete unit will be a pink circle, a purple square, and a blue triangle.

explore.label: Predictable or varied? Sort each design description.

cards.text: The same square tile repeated across a whole wall
Circle, square, triangle repeated in the same order forever
Circles whose colors, sizes, and thickness all vary across the canvas
You can name exactly what the next three shapes will be
The same shapes appear, but their size and order of appearance keep changing
A design with a clear pattern unit that repeats in a regular arrangement
The design has a flow, but you cannot predict what comes next
Concentric circles where the number of rings inside each circle varies

explore.instructions: Go deeper: Repetition and patterns have predictability — you know what comes next. Rhythm uses the same objects but varies their size, orientation, and order, so it often lacks predictability. After sorting, tell a partner which kind of design you find more visually appealing. As you work, ask yourself WHY it works.

connect.scenario: An artist's painting shows rows of circles. The colors and sizes of the circles vary, as does the number of concentric circles within each circle. The painting has rhythm.
connect.promptQuestion: How is a design with rhythm different from a pattern?
connect.prompt: The circle painting's colors and sizes ___, which is why it differs from a ___ — you cannot ___ what the next circle will look like.

check.stem: In the circle painting, the colors, sizes, and ring counts change from circle to circle with no repeating unit. What design element does this describe?
check.explanation: Rhythm is created by varying the placement, size, or order of the same objects. Repetition means one shape repeats exactly, a pattern unit is the repeating chunk of a pattern, and predictability is the trait a pattern has that this painting does not.

check.stem: Why can you NOT predict what the next circle in the painting will look like?
choices: Because rhythm varies color, size, and the number of rings instead of repeating a fixed unit
Because the artist used no shapes at all in the painting
Because the painting contains too many pattern units to count
Because circles are not allowed to be part of a geometric design
check.explanation: A pattern's predictability comes from a repeating unit; rhythm keeps the same object (a circle) but varies how it appears, so there is no fixed unit to predict from.

check.stem: A new row of circles is being added to the painting. Which addition keeps the design consistent with rhythm rather than turning it into a pattern?
choices: New circles with different colors, sizes, and ring counts than any existing row
An exact copy of the very first row, repeated precisely
Circles that follow a strict, repeating 3-shape unit
Replacing all the circles with a single repeated square
check.explanation: Rhythm continues by varying the same object in new ways, not by repeating an existing row exactly — an exact copy or a strict repeating unit would turn the design into a pattern instead.

connect.modelAnswer: The painting demonstrates rhythm because the colors, sizes, and thickness of the circles vary, as does the number of concentric circles inside each one. A pattern would repeat the same unit in a regular order, so I could predict the next circle exactly — with rhythm I cannot. A new row could use the same circles but in different sizes and colors, keeping the flow without copying any existing row.

onLevel.stem: The pattern unit circle-square-triangle repeats. What is shape number 12?
onLevel.explanation: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 with no remainder, so shape 12 ends a complete unit — the triangle, which is the last shape of the unit.
choiceFeedback: The circle is position 1 of a unit — that would need a remainder of 1, but 12 ÷ 3 has remainder 0.
The square is position 2 of a unit — that would need a remainder of 2, but 12 ÷ 3 has remainder 0.
It CAN be determined — a pattern's predictability is the point of the pattern unit.
hints: The unit is 3 shapes long. Divide 12 by 3.
12 ÷ 3 = 4 exactly, remainder 0.
No remainder means the LAST shape of the unit.

onLevel.stem: Same pattern. What is shape number 20?
choices: The 20th shape starts a new pattern
onLevel.explanation: 20 ÷ 3 = 6 remainder 2 (since 6 × 3 = 18 and 20 − 18 = 2), and the second shape in the unit is the purple square.
choiceFeedback: The circle needs a remainder of 1, but 20 − 18 = 2.
The triangle needs a remainder of 0, but 20 ÷ 3 leaves a remainder of 2.
The pattern never changes its unit — position 20 is still inside the same repeating pattern.
hints: How many complete units of 3 fit in 20?
6 units use 18 shapes; 20 − 18 = 2 left over.
Count 2 into the unit: circle, then ___ .

onLevel.stem: How many COMPLETE pattern units appear in the first 18 shapes of the circle-square-triangle border?
onLevel.explanation: Each unit is 3 shapes, and 18 ÷ 3 = 6 complete units.
choiceFeedback: That subtracts 18 − 3 instead of dividing.
That divides 18 by 2, but the unit has 3 shapes, not 2.
3 is the size of one unit, not the number of units in 18 shapes.
hints: One unit uses 3 shapes.
How many groups of 3 are in 18?
Divide 18 by 3.

onLevel.stem: A painting shows circles whose colors, sizes, and thickness vary, along with the number of concentric circles inside each one. Describe how the painting demonstrates rhythm.
onLevel.modelAnswer: The painting demonstrates rhythm because it uses the same object — a circle — but everything about how the circles appear varies: their colors, their sizes, their thickness, and how many rings sit inside each one. There is a flow, but no repeating unit you could use to predict the next circle.
sentenceStems: The painting uses the same object, but varies ___ .
It is rhythm and not a pattern because ___ .

extending.stem: How is a design with rhythm different from a pattern?
choices: Rhythm varies size, orientation, and order, so it often lacks predictability; a pattern repeats in a regular order
Rhythm uses shapes and a pattern does not
A pattern varies its shapes and rhythm never does
There is no difference between them
extending.explanation: A pattern repeats its unit in a regular arrangement, so it is predictable. Rhythm keeps the same objects but varies how they appear, giving flow without predictability.
choiceFeedback: Both use objects and shapes — the difference is in how they are arranged.
That is backwards: the PATTERN is the regular, predictable one, and rhythm is the one that varies.
They differ in exactly one important way: predictability.
hints: Think about predicting the next shape in each.
In which one can you always predict it?
A pattern is predictable; rhythm often is not.

extending.stem: If a new row of circles were added to the rhythm painting, what would they look like? Explain your thinking.
extending.modelAnswer: The new circles would still be circles, but their colors and sizes would vary and each would hold a different number of concentric rings — maybe a huge pale circle with many thin rings next to a small dark one with two thick rings. I cannot copy an existing row, because rhythm varies instead of repeating.
sentenceStems: The new row would keep ___ but vary ___ .

extending.stem: The circle-square-triangle pattern continues. What is shape number 25?
extending.explanation: 25 ÷ 3 = 8 remainder 1 (since 8 × 3 = 24 and 25 − 24 = 1), and the first shape of the unit is the pink circle.
choiceFeedback: The square needs a remainder of 2, but 25 − 24 = 1.
The triangle needs a remainder of 0, but 25 ÷ 3 leaves a remainder of 1.
A pattern is boundless — it continues, so shape 25 exists and is predictable.
hints: How many complete units of 3 fit in 25?
8 units use 24 shapes; 25 − 24 = 1 left over.
A remainder of 1 means the FIRST shape of the unit.

extending.stem: Which element of geometric design often LACKS predictability?
extending.explanation: Rhythm varies the size, orientation, and order of appearance of the same objects, so it gives flow but often lacks predictability.
choiceFeedback: Repetition is the MOST predictable element — one shape repeats exactly.
A pattern repeats its unit in a regular order, which is what makes it predictable.
The pattern unit is the source of a pattern's predictability, not something that lacks it.
hints: Which element varies size, orientation, and order?
Repetition and patterns both follow strict rules.
The one that varies is the unpredictable one.

extending.stem: Create a design that has repetition, pattern, AND rhythm. Describe (or sketch) it, and label where each element appears.
extending.modelAnswer: My design is a picture frame. The outer border is repetition: one gold square repeated all the way around. The inner border is a pattern: star, moon, star, moon in a regular order, so its pattern unit is 2 shapes. The center has rhythm: the same star shape scattered across the middle in different sizes, angles, and colors, so it flows but cannot be predicted.
sentenceStems: My pattern's unit is ___ , and my rhythm varies ___ .

extending.stem: Why do you think the lesson is called 'Math is Boundless'? Use repetition, pattern, and rhythm in your answer.
extending.modelAnswer: A pattern unit can repeat forever — there is no last circle, square, or triangle, so the design has no boundary. Repetition can cover any wall, patterns let us predict shape 25 or shape 25,000, and rhythm shows that even without predictability, math ideas keep creating endless new designs. The designs, like math, never have to end.
sentenceStems: Rhythm shows math is boundless because ___ .

extending.stem: In geometric design, what is repetition?
choices: The same object or shape repeated multiple times
A set of different shapes arranged randomly
Shapes that vary in size and order of appearance
extending.explanation: Repetition involves one repeated object, shape, or form — and because of that, it has predictability.
choiceFeedback: A random arrangement has no rule, so it is neither repetition nor a pattern.
Varying size and order describes rhythm, not repetition.
Color alone does not make a design element — repetition is about a repeated shape.
hints: The word itself is a clue: something repeats.
How many different objects does repetition involve?
One object or shape, repeated multiple times.

extending.stem: A border shows: pink circle, purple square, blue triangle, pink circle, purple square, blue triangle. What are the next three shapes?
choices: Pink circle, purple square, blue triangle
Blue triangle, purple square, pink circle
Pink circle, blue triangle, purple square
extending.explanation: The pattern unit is circle, square, triangle, so it repeats in the same order: a pink circle, a purple square, and a blue triangle.
choiceFeedback: That reverses the unit — a pattern repeats in the SAME order, not backwards.
That swaps the square and triangle; the unit's order never changes.
A pattern has predictability — that is exactly what makes it a pattern.
hints: Find the chunk that repeats.
The unit is circle, square, triangle.
After a triangle, the unit starts over.

practice.commonMistake: Calling every repeated design a 'pattern.' One identical shape repeated is repetition; a pattern needs a unit of shapes repeating in a regular order; and rhythm varies the shapes' size and order, so it is neither.

exitTicket.stem: Explain your thinking — Which statement best matches this lesson's summary of 'Math is Boundless'?
choices: Math can be used to create beautiful designs, which often have repetition, patterns, and rhythm
Designs only count as mathematical if they are perfectly predictable
Rhythm is the only real element of design
exitTicket.explanation: The summary names all three elements — repetition, patterns, and rhythm — as the ways math creates beautiful, endless designs.
hints: Look back at the Summarize slide.
It names three elements of design.
Which option includes all three?

parallelPractice.stem: A square pyramid has base edge 6 and slant height 2. Find its total surface area.

steps.prompt: Add the base and all side faces: ___.
steps.promptEs: Suma la base y todas las caras laterales: ___.

hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Use the visual model, then complete one step at a time.
Start like this: Find the square base: 6 × 6 = 36.
parallelPractice.explanation: Find the square base: 6 × 6 = 36. Find one triangular face: 1/2 × 6 × 2 = 6. Find all 4 triangular faces: 4 × 6 = 24. Add the base and all side faces: 60.
parallelPractice.stemEs: Una pirámide de base cuadrada tiene arista de la base 6 y altura inclinada 2. Encuentra su área de superficie total.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
Usa el modelo visual y completa un paso a la vez.
Empieza así: Encuentra la base cuadrada: 6 × 6 = 36.
parallelPractice.explanationEs: Encuentra la base cuadrada: 6 × 6 = 36. Encuentra una cara triangular: 1/2 × 6 × 2 = 6. Encuentra las 4 caras triangulares: 4 × 6 = 24. Suma la base y todas las caras laterales: 60.
